objectives: Hear /b/ followed immediately by /r/ at the beginning of a taught word.
Blend the two consonant sounds smoothly without inserting a vowel.
Distinguish the /br/ onset from /b/ alone and from other taught blends.
Say a complete word after blending its onset and rime.
concepts: The initial br blend contains two consonant phonemes /b/ and /r/ in that order.
Both sounds are heard; no extra vowel belongs between them.
A blend preserves each consonant sound while the sounds move together.
Listening, saying, and checking the whole word supports accurate decoding.

definitions.definition: Two consonant sounds heard together at the beginning of a word.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.
To join speech sounds in order to say a word.

workedExamples.solution: Blend without adding a vowel: brick.

workedExamples.prompt: Compare /b/ and /br/ at the start of a word.
workedExamples.solution: The /br/ onset has both /b/ and /r/; /b/ alone omits /r/.
Hear /b/, then /r/, then the remaining sounds /ʌ/ /ʃ/.

commonMistakes: Saying buh-rick instead of blending /b/ and /r/ smoothly.
Dropping /r/ and saying a word as if it began with /b/ alone.
Naming letter names instead of producing speech sounds.
Guessing a word before listening to all its sounds.
keyTakeaways: Do not add a vowel between the consonants.
Blend the onset with the rest of the word.
Check that the complete word matches the sounds heard.
revisionPoints: Brick and brush both begin with br.
Do not insert a vowel between /b/ and /r/.
Listen to the whole word before answering.
